figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1. Outline of the Taxol biosynthetic pathway. Hydroxylation of the committed precursor taxa-4(5),11(12)-diene to taxadien-5a-ol by the taxoid
5a-hydroxylase (A), hydroxylation of taxadien-5a-ol by the taxoid 13a-hydroxylase (B), acetylation of taxadien-5a-ol by the taxadienol-O-
acetyltransferase (TAX1 or TAX19) (C), hydroxylation of taxadien-5a-yl acetate by the taxoid 10b-hydroxylase (D), acetylation of 10-
deacetylbaccatin III (10-DAB) by the 10-DAB-10-O-acetyltransferase (TAX6) (E), and the side chain attachment to baccatin III to form Taxol (F)
are depicted. Broken arrows indicate multiple steps, several of which remain undeﬁned.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2. A postulated biosynthetic scheme for oxetane ring formation in late-stage taxoids. The 4(20)-ene-5a-ol functional grouping is converted to the
4(20)-ene-5a-yl acetate, followed by epoxidation to the corresponding 4(20)b-epoxy-5a-acetoxy derivative, and then intramolecular rearrangement to
the 4a-acetoxy-4,5b-oxetane moiety.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3. Deduced amino acid sequence alignment of taxoid acetyltransferases: TAX19 (taxoid 5a-acetyltransferase), TAX1 (previously identiﬁed
taxoid 5a-acetyltransferase), TAX14 (taxadien-5a,13a-diol and 5a,10b-diol acyltransferase), and TAX6 (10-DAB-10-O-acetyltransferase). Black
boxes indicate identical residues; grey boxes indicate identical residues for at least two of the sequences. The conserved motifs are indicated above the
alignment.
